title: One-variable fields over a separably closed field
statement:
If $F$ is separably closed, then
$\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(F(x))\leq1$, with the bound of
[def-sc-etale-torsion-cd].

proof.text: Index by finite subsets $S\subset F[x]\setminus\{0\}$ ordered by inclusion, and put $h_S=\prod_{h\in S}h$ (empty product $1$) and $X_S=\operatorname{Spec}F[x,1/h_S]$. For $S\subset T$, the inclusion of localizations gives a transition map $X_T\to X_S$. Every fraction $a/b\in F(x)$ belongs to the stage $S=\{b\}$, so the filtered colimit of these rings is $F(x)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit] (which also makes every transition map affine) $\varprojlim_S X_S=\operatorname{Spec}F(x)$. Each stage is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs].

Write $L=\overline F$. In characteristic zero every irreducible polynomial is separable, hence linear over the separably closed field $F$, so $L=F$. In characteristic $p>0$, the minimal polynomial of any $a\in L$ has the form $g(T^{p^r})$ with $g$ irreducible and separable; $g$ is linear, so $a^{p^r}\in F$. Here is the universal-homeomorphism check from [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]: for any $F$-algebra $R$, the map $R\to B=R\otimes_F L$ is injective (extend $1$ to an $F$-basis of $L$), and each $b\in B$ has a power $b^{p^n}\in R$, by choosing one exponent for its finitely many coefficients in $L$. A prime $P\subset R$ therefore has exactly one prime above it, namely $Q_P=\{b\in B:b^{p^n}\in P\text{ for an exponent with }b^{p^n}\in R\}$: independence of exponent and the ideal and prime properties follow by taking a common exponent and using Frobenius and primality of $P$. Under this bijection $D_B(b)$ corresponds to $D_R(b^{p^n})$, so it is a homeomorphism. Checking on affine opens of an arbitrary base change proves that $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}F$, and consequently $X_S\times_F\operatorname{Spec}L\to X_S$, are universal homeomorphisms. By [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance] their pullback equivalences preserve cohomology. On abelian sheaves these equivalences are exact and preserve torsion (a torsion sheaf is the filtered union of the kernels of multiplication by $n!$, and an additive equivalence preserves those kernels and their colimit); thus vanishing for every torsion sheaf in degrees $q>1$ is equivalent on the two schemes, as in [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd].

The base change of $X_S$ is $\operatorname{Spec}L[x,1/h_S]$. Since $F\to L$ is injective, $h_S$ stays nonzero. This algebra is generated over $L$ by $x$ and $1/h_S$, so the scheme is of finite type; it is separated since the diagonal of an affine scheme over a field is induced by the surjective multiplication map $A\otimes_L A\to A$. The Euclidean domain $L[x]$ has only the zero prime and maximal nonzero primes, so localization has dimension at most one. Hence all hypotheses of [lem-sc-arbitrary-curve-cd] hold with $e=1$, giving $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(X_S\times_F\operatorname{Spec}L)\leq1$. Step 2 gives $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(X_S)\leq1$, in the sense of [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd].

source.place: ## Proof, “Over F̄ the bound is one ...”

proof.text: The finite-subset index is filtered (use $S\cup T$), every $X_S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and every transition map is affine, as checked in step 1. Step 3 gives the uniform bound $c=1$. Thus [lem-sc-cd-affine-limit] applies to $\varprojlim_S X_S=\operatorname{Spec}F(x)$ and gives $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(\operatorname{Spec}F(x))\leq1$, which is precisely the asserted field bound by [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd].

split_report.summary: Audited the imported one-paragraph route. No new nodes were needed: the localization/inverse-limit description is elementary, while the three substantive inputs are existing nodes. Expanded the proof into four steps, made the universal-homeomorphism transfer and the affine-curve hypotheses explicit, and added the required Mathlib search record. Second reading supplied the prime-ideal and basic-open argument for universal homeomorphisms, an explicit filtered index and all curve/limit hypotheses; corrected citation quotations.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the entire proof paragraph of the blueprint node: localization stages, purely inseparable algebraic-closure base change, the affine-curve bound, and passage to the fraction field via lem-sc-cd-affine-limit.

tool_uses.why: Generic invariance of the etale topos and cohomology under a universal homeomorphism is needed for the purely inseparable algebraic-closure base change. The blueprint itself cites this tool from sk-prop-cd, and sk-prop-sf-cbc has no statement supplying it. This is a proposal for the maintainer, not an accepted top-level tool_uses record.
